overview: Every other distance sensor in this encyclopedia looks in one direction. An RPLIDAR spins a laser rangefinder continuously, taking thousands of distance readings per second across a full 360-degree sweep, producing a complete 2D map of everything around the robot with each rotation. That's the sensor that makes real SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) possible on a hobbyist budget — it's the standard entry point for anyone moving from 'avoid the wall in front of me' navigation into 'build a live map of the room and know where I am in it.' It needs noticeably more from the rest of the system than a single-point sensor: a spinning motor to power, a serial connection fast enough for the data stream, and usually a Raspberry Pi or similar (not a bare Arduino) to run the SLAM software that turns the point cloud into a usable map.
simpleSummary: A spinning sensor that scans distance all around it, building a 360-degree map instead of looking one way.

specifications.operatingVoltage: 5V (logic/communication), separate motor supply on some models
specifications.samplesPerScan: Hundreds to a few thousand distance points per rotation
specifications.interface: UART serial (often via a USB adapter for PC/Pi connection)
specifications.angularResolution: ~1° or finer depending on model and scan rate

pinMap.name: Motor+
pinMap.function: Power for the internal motor that spins the scanning head.
pinMap.gotcha: Motor speed affects scan rate and data timing — most SLAM software expects a specific, stable rotation speed.

pinMap.name: TX
pinMap.function: Serial transmit — streams distance/angle data to the host.
pinMap.gotcha: The data rate is high enough that a software-emulated serial port on a slow microcontroller will drop data — a real hardware UART (or USB adapter to a Pi/PC) is strongly preferred.

pinMap.name: RX
pinMap.function: Serial receive — accepts start/stop scan commands from the host.

useCases.title: SLAM-based autonomous navigation
useCases.scenario: Build a live map of a room while simultaneously tracking the robot's position within it — the core capability behind robot vacuums and autonomous mobile robots.

useCases.title: 360° obstacle field for path planning
useCases.scenario: Feed the full point-cloud sweep into a path-planning algorithm for smoother navigation than single-point sensors allow.

oftenConfusedWith: HC-SR04/VL53L0X (single-point sensors, no rotation, no mapping capability)
oftenUpgradedTo: 3D LiDAR units (add vertical scanning planes for full 3D point clouds)
